Definition: properly, to twist as a rope; to bound (as by a line)
BiblicalUsage: Gabal means to set a bound, to draw the line that must not be crossed. God told Moses to set bounds around Mount Sinai in Exodus 19:12, and the law forbids removing a neighbour's landmark in Deuteronomy 19:14. The Jordan was the border of Benjamin's inheritance in Joshua 18:20, and Hamath also shall border on Tyre and Zidon in Zechariah 9:2.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God's bounds are a kindness, not a cage. The line around Sinai kept the people alive, and the landmark kept a neighbour's field his own. I hold that the boundaries God sets are the fences of a good Father.
